title: Active and Passive Voice
description: Master active and passive voice for Grade 8: formation in all tenses, special constructions, and when to use the passive — with bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: How to Change Active to Passive
topics.concept:
Follow three steps to turn an active sentence into a passive one:

  1. Move the object to the front (it becomes the new subject).
  2. Change the verb to the correct form of be (in the same tense) + the past participle (V3).
  3. Put the old subject after by (drop it if unknown or obvious).

Active: The dog (subject) chased the cat (object).
Passive: The cat was chased by the dog.

The tense never changes — only the form of 'be' carries it. Present → is/are; past → was/were; future → will be; perfect → has/have been.

examples.problem: Change to passive: The teacher praised the students.
examples.solution: The students were praised by the teacher. — past tense → 'were' + 'praised' (V3).

examples.problem: Change to passive: They are building a house.
examples.solution: A house is being built (by them). — present continuous passive = is/are being + V3.

recap: Object → subject; verb → be (same tense) + V3; subject → by + object
The tense is carried by the form of 'be'
Drop 'by …' when the doer is unknown or obvious

topics.title: Special Passive Constructions
topics.concept:
Some sentences need extra care:

  • Two objects: 'He gave me a book' → two passives: I was given a book / A book was given to me.
  • With modals: 'You must do the work' → The work must be done. (modal + be + V3)
  • Impersonal passive: 'People say he is rich' → It is said that he is rich.
  • Passive infinitive: 'She wants someone to invite her' → She wants to be invited.
  • Passive with 'get': informal — He got hurt / The window got broken.
  • Imperatives: 'Shut the door' → Let the door be shut.

examples.problem: Passive with a modal: We should respect elders.
examples.solution: Elders should be respected. — modal 'should' + be + V3.

examples.problem: Impersonal passive: People believe that she is honest.
examples.solution: It is believed that she is honest.

recap: Two objects → two possible passive forms
Modals: modal + be + V3 (must be done)
Impersonal: It is said/believed that …; imperatives: Let … be + V3

intro.en: In the active voice, the subject does the action: "The chef cooked the meal." In the passive voice, the subject receives the action: "The meal was cooked by the chef." The passive shifts the spotlight from the doer to the thing done — useful when the doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious.
intro.hi: कर्तृवाच्य (active voice) में कर्ता क्रिया करता है: "The chef cooked the meal." कर्मवाच्य (passive voice) में कर्ता क्रिया पाता है: "The meal was cooked by the chef." Passive ध्यान करने वाले से हटाकर हुई वस्तु पर ले जाता है — तब उपयोगी जब करने वाला अज्ञात, अमहत्वपूर्ण या स्पष्ट हो।

real_life.situation:
You read a notice and a news headline:

Notice: The library will be closed tomorrow.

News: A new bridge has been built over the river.
real_life.why: Neither sentence names who closes the library or who built the bridge — because it doesn't matter, or everyone knows. That is exactly when the passive voice is the natural, professional choice: formal notices, science, and news.
